paragraphs: The train [[descended|descend]] into the valley after dusk, and the [[flat]] roof of the old station looked exactly as it had ten years before. I had [[departed|depart]] from the city with more [[sorrow]] than I expected, and I still [[grieve]] for the office I left behind. There was [[regret]], too, for the colleagues I never properly thanked. My cousin met me in a [[rental]] car, the only vehicle we could [[afford]] that week.

On Monday I started at a small [[firm]] that had spent twenty years repairing old buildings. It was not a famous [[establishment]], but the local [[agency]] trusted it, and the culture [[department]] sent work our way. My [[commute]] was a [[regular]] twelve-minute walk along the river. The pay was [[modest]], and I could only [[present]] a trainee's portfolio, but I was glad to be home. The [[prime]] reason I took the job was the old theater at the end of the street.

The theater was a [[compact]] brick [[structure]] with a leaking roof and an empty stage. Half of its [[material]] was original timber, and the [[cement]] in the back wall had [[sunk|sink]] in places. [[Moisture]] had crept into the basement, and the damp had [[aggravated|aggravate]] every crack. A [[severe]] winter two years earlier had done [[disastrous]] damage to the north wing. Rubble [[obstructed|obstruct]] the side entrance, so we had to [[fend]] our way through the yard. The [[renovation]] would be expensive, and nobody wanted to [[overstate]] what we could finish by June.

The caretaker, Mr. Gu, had a [[literary]] way of speaking and a thick local [[dialect]]. He could [[relate]] every crack in the wall to an [[episode]] in the theater's history. His storytelling was a kind of [[worship]] of the old actors, and I began to [[trace]] their names on the dressing-room wall. That habit was an old [[tradition]] in this town, he said, and it mattered more than any official record. On one door a child had written the [[alphabet]] in chalk, and he kept an [[analogue]] tape recorder beside it to save the songs. He refused to let anyone [[destruct]] the old projector, and he [[remarked|remark]] that the town had once been famous for its [[classical]] music.

In February the heating pipes [[flared|flare]] and then burst, which was completely [[unexpected]]. The flood [[induced|induce]] a wave of doubt among the volunteers. The most [[desperate]] ones worked all night to [[relieve]] the pressure on the pumps. I [[tolerated|tolerate]] the cold for six hours before going home to sleep in my coat. The volunteers needed [[intensive]] training before they could handle the pumps alone. There is a particular [[misery]] in watching water rise over work you have just finished.

Before we could touch the facade, we needed [[permission]] from the city. The [[procedure]] was slow: an [[enquiry]] at the planning office, a formal [[inquiry]] into the building's status, and weeks of waiting. New [[legislation]] protected historic sites, but the [[agency]] that enforced it was short of staff. Mr. Gu [[insisted|insist]] that we [[uphold]] the original design, and his argument [[prevailed|prevail]]. The theater had a [[monopoly]] on memories in this town, he said, and that counted for something.

Then a letter from a major [[shareholder]] arrived: the developer wanted to [[convert]] the hall into a car park. Their lawyer was [[aggressive]] and [[overstated|overstate]] the [[proceeds]] of a new shopping centre. The glossy brochures [[inflated|inflate]] the value of the developer's [[brand]] and ignored the town entirely. They [[misinterpreted|misinterpret]] the heritage report, or perhaps they only [[pretended|pretend]] to. The company tried to [[induce]] the council to sell, and I grew [[pessimistic]] about our chances. The [[circumstances|circumstance]] looked hopeless, every [[ally]] seemed tired, and I began to see the whole affair as a [[dilemma]] with no clean answer.

The [[press]] came to the emergency meeting, and a local station agreed to [[broadcast]] it live. Each speaker had to [[affirm]] the [[intention]] behind the plan, which raised awkward questions of [[ethics]]. One councillor questioned the [[integrity]] of the developer's figures, and the room went quiet. Given the [[amount]] of public support, the council voted to [[safeguard]] the building. [[Propaganda]] had filled the room for weeks, but in the end the facts won.

That night I [[estimated|estimate]] the cost of repairs and [[allocated|allocate]] the work among three teams. From the old photographs I could [[infer]] how the stage once looked, and I [[analysed|analyse]] the paint samples. My colleague chose to [[analyze|analyze]] the sound records instead. The report had [[multiple]] appendices: a [[chronology]] of repairs, an [[updated]] list of donors, and every [[detail]] of the damaged roof. Above all, it was [[essential]] to [[prevent]] water from reaching the archive, and we had to [[finalize]] the budget before Friday.

On Sundays I helped in the community garden, where [[moisture]] in the soil decided what would grow. The children recorded every [[insect]] they found and [[hunted|hunt]] for beetles under the stones. The old bus in town ran on [[biofuel]] made from used cooking oil. A single [[molecule]] of detergent can poison a pond, the teacher said, so we washed our tools in a bucket. The garden was our only [[recreation]], and it kept us sane through the spring.

My aunt had waited two years for a kidney [[transplant]]. The local [[institute]] ran a small dialysis unit with four beds. A [[shortage]] of nurses meant she was often still waiting at midnight. Her file was thick with [[correspondence]] between two hospitals that never read each other's notes. Some of her treatment was still [[undocumented]] because the clinic had no digital system. I spent an afternoon trying to [[rectify]] a mistake in her record, and a [[drastic]] change of diet had kept her alive.

In the studio we [[persisted|persist]] with the original plan, even when the money ran low. A [[prominent]] architect visited and said the hall was [[unsurpassed]] as an example of small-town Art Deco. Her [[philosophy]] was simple: repair first, replace last. We would [[replace]] only the beams that could not be [[rendered|render]] safe. A [[substance]] in the old paint turned out to be poisonous, which made the work slower. We [[equipped|equip]] every team with masks and gloves, and had to [[modify]] the schedule and [[alter]] the roof pitch.

The [[innovation]] was to [[establish]] a small workshop where local teenagers could learn carpentry. The workshop proved more [[beneficial]] than any lecture about heritage. Old skills [[derive]] from practice, not from slogans. The change would [[transform]] the way the town thought about its own past. At first the change was [[intangible]], a matter of pride rather than money.

In May the city [[philharmonic]] agreed to play a [[charity]] concert in the unfinished hall. My [[desire]] to hear a full orchestra in that dusty space was almost childish. We set up a [[lounge]] in the foyer with borrowed sofas, and someone ran a [[quiz]] at the interval. The concert had a [[mass]] appeal that no advertisement could buy. The [[proceeds]] from the tickets paid for half the roof.

On the last free weekend we drove to the coast, where I tried to [[surf]] on a borrowed board. We [[offloaded|offload]] the boards from the van and carried them down the beach. For an hour I did nothing but [[lounge]] on the sand and watch the water. The [[release]] from tension was [[prompt]] and complete. I felt [[bound]] to return to the theater, though, before dark.

That evening my aunt showed me a box of photographs of our [[ancestors|ancestor]]. [[Prior]] to the war, one of them had been a stagehand at the very same theater. That story [[represented|represent]] everything the renovation was about. A town that forgets its people, she said, has no [[substance]]. [[Humanity]] survives in small acts of repair.

The [[recession]] had hit the region hard, and the [[environment]] for small projects was poor. Yet the council [[deputed|depute]] my supervisor to [[inform]] the developer that the plan was dead. The decision would [[pave]] the way for slower, more careful growth. It would [[influence]] other towns facing the same choice.
